question: What does human embryology focus on studying?

options.B: Growth and aging processes in older adults
options.C: Development from a zygote up to the eighth week
options.D: Nutritional needs of a lactating mother

explanation: You're doing great! Embryology simply looks at how a baby develops from fertilization all the way to the end of the eighth week. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h1)

question: What does the medical term 'teratology' study?

options.B: Normal rate of placental weight gain

explanation: Don't let the big word scare you! Teratology is just the study of birth defects and what causes them. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h1)

question: How many functional sperm cells are produced from one primary spermatocyte?
explanation: Spot on! The process of making sperm (spermatogenesis) neatly divides to give you four healthy, working sperm cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h2)

question: What is a major difference between making eggs (oogenesis) and making sperm (spermatogenesis)?

options.B: Oogenesis continues actively throughout old age
options.C: Oogenesis produces only one functional ovum

explanation: You've got this! While sperm production gives four equal cells, egg production focuses its energy to create just one big, strong egg and a few tiny helper cells. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h2)

question: In which part of the female reproductive system does fertilization usually take place?

options.D: Cervical os of the lower uterus

explanation: That's right! The sperm and egg usually meet and fuse in the wider middle section of the fallopian tube called the ampulla. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h3)

question: Why is the cortical reaction so important right after fertilization?

options.A: It determines the biological sex of the baby
options.B: It prevents any extra sperm from entering the egg
options.C: It helps the embryo implant in the womb
options.D: It triggers immediate rapid mitotic division

explanation: Think of the cortical reaction as a security guard—it quickly locks the door so only one sperm can fertilize the egg! [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h3)

question: What do we call the solid ball of 12 to 16 cells that forms early in development?
explanation: Brilliant! Because this little cluster of cells looks a bit like a tiny mulberry, we call it the morula. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h4)

question: What does the inner cell mass of a blastocyst turn into?
explanation: Exactly! The inner cell mass is the special group of cells that will grow into the actual body of the baby. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h4)

question: Which hormone is released by the early trophoblast to keep the corpus luteum working?
explanation: Well done! hCG is the famous hormone pregnancy tests look for, and it tells the body to keep making progesterone to protect the pregnancy. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h5)

question: What is the main job of the syncytiotrophoblast during implantation?

options.A: Invading the maternal endometrium and blood vessels
options.B: Creating the protective fluid-filled amniotic cavity
options.C: Preventing multiple sperm from entering the oocyte
options.D: Forming the internal organs of the growing fetus

explanation: You're doing great! This outer layer acts like a tiny pioneer, helping the blastocyst burrow safely into the lining of the womb. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h5)

question: During gastrulation, the embryonic disc forms how many primary tissue layers?
explanation: Spot on! Gastrulation sets up three foundational layers (ectoderm, mesoderm, and endoderm) from which all body organs will grow. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which part of the body mainly develops from the embryonic ectoderm?
explanation: That's correct! The ectoderm forms the outer parts of us, including our skin and our entire brain and spinal cord. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h6)

question: Why is an embryo most at risk from harmful substances during weeks four to eight?

options.A: Major organ systems are actively forming
options.B: The placenta has not yet begun functioning
options.C: Rapid maternal weight gain puts stress on cells
options.D: The fetal kidneys start producing waste products

explanation: You've got this! Because the baby's major organs are rapidly under construction during this time, they are very sensitive to outside harm. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h7)

question: During which stage of pregnancy do most major structural birth defects happen?
explanation: Brilliant! Since organs are actively being built during weeks one through eight (the embryonic period), disturbances here cause major structural issues. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h8)

question: A pregnant patient asks why she must avoid harmful drugs in early pregnancy. What is the best nursing reply?

options.A: Major organs are forming and easily damaged then
options.B: Maternal liver failure causes direct fetal poisoning
options.C: Placental hormones do not filter toxins until term
options.D: The baby drinks amniotic fluid that traps chemicals

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Explaining that major organs are forming right now helps the patient understand why early caution is so vital. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T6#GNS111_U1_T6_h8)
